# EQ Universal Agent Principles

These four sections are **constraints, not suggestions**. They are auto-prepended to every agent spec in this repo. If a task asks you to violate one, you stop and surface the conflict — you do not silently comply. Each principle ties to a guardrail doc that is the source of truth when there is doubt.

> Read order for any build agent: these principles → your agent spec → the task. Run `dna-precheck` before generating, `self-evaluate` before handing off. No exceptions.

> **Lineage.** These are the **Andrej Karpathy** school of agentic coding — *think before you code, simplicity first, surgical changes* — made operational for the EQ estate. In eq-sparks they are realised through the **autoresearch (A-Rag) loop** ([`../methodology/autoresearch-loop.md`](../methodology/autoresearch-loop.md)) — the canonical restate → search → read → hypothesise → act → verify cycle every agent runs — and gated by the **`self-evaluate`** skill, which grades each output-producing pass against its Done Criteria before anything hands off. Principles §1–§4 are *what* good work looks like; §5 is the *loop* that proves it.

---

## 1. Think before you code

> Tied to: **safety-rails** (refuse-on-ambiguity), **path-policy** (every change maps to a real file).

You MUST, before writing or editing a single line:

- **Restate the task in your own words** — one or two sentences. If you cannot restate it, you do not understand it yet; ask `@decision` to resolve the ambiguity rather than guessing.
- **List your assumptions explicitly.** Anything not stated in the PBI / acceptance criteria (ACs) / contract is an assumption and must be written down so `@critic` and the human can see it.
- **Never invent requirements.** If an AC is silent on a behaviour, you do not add it. Scope creep is a `@critic` FAIL. Resolve genuine forks through `@decision`, which records a defensible rationale in the run log — you do not decide unilaterally.
- **Stop if you cannot map the task to concrete files.** If you cannot name the target file(s) and the repo they live in (an MFE, `eq-one-shared`, `eq-one-design-system`, or a `src/domains/<name>/` BFF folder), the task is not ready. Escalate to `@architect` (placement) or `@decision` (ambiguity) instead of creating files on a hunch — that is a **path-policy** violation.

The cost angle: thinking is cheap, rework is not. A clear restatement up front is what lets a HAIKU/SONNET agent succeed on the first pass instead of burning escalation budget on a confused second attempt.

---

## 2. Simplicity first

> Tied to: **budget-policy** (cheapest correct solution wins), **model-routing-policy** (don't manufacture complexity that forces escalation).

- **Write the minimum code that satisfies the ACs — nothing more.** No "while I'm here" features, no speculative configurability.
- **No premature abstraction.** Do not introduce a base class, generic, hook, or helper for a single caller. Abstract only when the second real use case exists (and when it does, that shared code moves to `eq-one-shared` — see §4).
- **Comment only the non-obvious WHY.** Do not narrate WHAT the code does — the code already says that. Explain a non-obvious decision, a downstream constraint, or a workaround. Redundant comments are noise that `@reviewer` will flag.
- **Prefer the boring, well-trodden path** the codebase already uses over a cleverer one you would have to justify.

The cost angle: simplicity keeps you on your default model tier. Self-invented complexity drives down self-eval confidence and triggers an escalation rung you didn't need — a direct hit to the run budget tracked by `budget-check`.

---

## 3. Surgical changes

> Tied to: **safety-rails** (smallest reversible change), **path-policy** (stay inside the blast radius you declared).

- **Match the existing style** of the file and module you are touching — naming, formatting, imports, file layout, test structure. The diff should look like the person who wrote the file wrote it.
- **Keep every diff reviewable in under 60 seconds.** If a change cannot be reviewed at a glance, split it. Large, sprawling diffs are where `@critic` and `@security` lose the thread and bugs hide.
- **Do not refactor orthogonal code.** Touch only what the ACs require. Tidying unrelated code, renaming things you happened to read, or reformatting whole files is out of scope and will FAIL review — it bloats the diff and the budget. If you spot genuine dead or duplicated code, flag it for `@scanner` / `@shared-curator` rather than fixing it inline.
- **Make changes reversible.** Prefer additive, narrowly-scoped edits over rewrites so a single revert undoes your work cleanly.

The cost angle: tight diffs make the OPUS-tier gates (`@critic`, `@security`, `@architect`) fast and accurate, so the platform spends its most expensive tokens on judgment, not on wading through churn.

---

## 4. EQ cross-repo DNA

> Tied to: **dedup-policy** (REUSE > EXTEND > CREATE), **cache-policy** (reuse cached pre-check results), **path-policy** (correct repo/folder placement).

This is what makes eq-sparks an *EQ* harness and not a generic coder. Non-negotiable:

- **ALWAYS run `dna-precheck` first.** Before generating any code, the cross-repo DNA pre-check classifies the work as reuse / extend / create by inspecting all FE repos and the BFF. Skipping it is a hard **dedup-policy** violation. Its result is cacheable per **cache-policy** — reuse the lookup, never re-scan blindly.
- **Honour reuse precedence: REUSE > EXTEND > CREATE.** If equivalent code exists, consume it. If something close exists, extend it. Only create when nothing fits — and say why in your handoff. Creating a near-duplicate is the single most expensive mistake in this estate.
- **Common code MOVES to `eq-one-shared`.** Layout, auth, common API clients, common Zustand stores, anything reused across MFEs lives in `eq-one-shared` — never duplicated into `eq-one-saye-mfe`, `eq-one-sip-mfe`, or `eq-one-shares-mfe`. When you find duplication, route it to `@shared-curator` (via `move-to-shared`), don't copy-paste.
- **UI consumes `eq-one-design-system`.** Never hand-roll a component the design system already provides (it is the facade over the `eq-one-studio` Storybook). `@design-system` BLOCKS hand-rolled equivalents.
- **FE matches the ExperienceAPI contract.** Frontend types and clients track the BFF's published per-domain OpenAPI/Swagger contract. On any FE↔BFF boundary, defer to `@contract` (and `contract-diff`); drift is a FAIL.
- **Respect MFE boundaries.** Child MFEs are independent — they MUST NOT reach into each other or duplicate each other's code. Cross-MFE wiring goes through the `eq-nexus-ui` RootMFE shell and its module-federation contract (`@mfe`'s domain). BFF domains under `src/domains/<name>/` are independently deployable and stay decoupled; the BFF paints & polishes shapes, it does not hold business logic.

The cost angle: no-repeat is the whole point. Every reuse avoided is generation, review, and test budget saved — and a smaller estate to maintain for the 20–50 developers downstream.

---

## 5. Research, don't guess — and prove it

> Tied to: **dedup-policy** (DNA pre-check + idempotent task ledger — never repeat work), **budget-policy** (the loop is bounded; `self-evaluate` confidence drives escalation).

Principles §1–§4 say *what* good work looks like; this one is the *loop* that produces and proves it. It is the operational core of the Karpathy method — you research your way to the change, you do not guess it.

- **Follow the autoresearch (A-Rag) loop.** Every output-producing pass runs the canonical cycle in [`../methodology/autoresearch-loop.md`](../methodology/autoresearch-loop.md): **restate** the task and list assumptions (§1) → **search** to locate (don't bulk-read the repo) → **read** narrowly through the cache → **hypothesise** the change in writing → **act** with a surgical edit (§2–§3) → **verify** against evidence. `loop: autoresearch` agents iterate the converge loop within budget; `loop: single-shot` agents do one focused pass. You never skip straight from task to code.
- **End every output-producing pass with `self-evaluate`.** This is mandatory, not optional. `writesDiff` agents run the diff-based `self-evaluate` skill as their final step — each Done Criterion marked PASS/FAIL with concrete evidence and a confidence score. Read-only / gate / planning agents self-*assess* their report's completeness and confidence instead (an empty diff must never read as FAIL). Confidence below **0.7** — or two `@critic` FAILs — gates the one-rung escalation in *Before you hand off*.
- **Hand off via a structured envelope — never free text.** When a pass is done, compose with the next agent through the `handoff` protocol ([`../methodology/handoff-protocol.md`](../methodology/handoff-protocol.md)): a structured envelope (task, hypothesis, decisions, artifacts reuse/extend/create, files touched, `self_eval`, open items, budget, next) written via the `handoff` skill. The orchestrator routes it; `@supervisor` aggregates every envelope into the Summary. Prose summaries lose decisions and confidence — the envelope does not.
- **Never repeat work.** Before generating, `dna-precheck` classifies each artifact REUSE / EXTEND / CREATE across the estate (§4); during a run, the idempotent **task ledger** records each task done/pending/blocked so `/resume` skips what is already `done`. Re-doing settled work — or re-scanning instead of reusing a cached pre-check — is a **dedup-policy** waste, not diligence.

The cost angle: the loop *is* the cost control. Researching before acting, proving each pass with `self-evaluate`, and refusing to repeat settled work is what keeps agents on their default tier and the run inside its `budget-check` ceiling — guessing burns the budget twice.

---

## Before you hand off

You are not done until you have run **`self-evaluate`**. If your self-eval confidence is below **0.7**, or you have taken two `@critic` FAILs, you may escalate exactly **one model rung** per **model-routing-policy** — logged and budgeted. You never auto-downgrade, and you never escalate to dodge doing the thinking in §1.
